title: Tell Menippus to Come Down
description: Diogenes catches Polydeuces on his way back to the upper world and loads him with errands: invite Menippus down for better laughs, tell the philosophers to shut up, tell the rich to stop hoarding, tell the beautiful that beauty is dust. Polydeuces takes it all in stride — until Diogenes starts in on the Spartans, at which point he draws a line. A brisk opening: the show's worldview delivered as a delivery list. Cast: Diogenes, Polydeuces.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil illustration. Dark stone columns frame a torchlit threshold between the underworld and a faint daylight beyond. Diogenes — gravelly old Cynic in a tattered cloak — stands close to camera dictating, one finger raised, the scrappy brass-lanterned Cynic dog at his heel. Polydeuces, a clean-limbed young athlete in a simple white chiton with a faint divine glow, listens patiently with a half-smile. Warm torch-light against deep navy shadow. Strong central two-shot composition that reads at thumbnail size.

title: Bad Neighbours
description: Croesus files a formal noise complaint with Pluto: Menippus keeps laughing while he and Midas and Sardanapalus are trying to lament properly. Pluto, weary, hears both sides. Menippus cheerfully promises to keep singing 'Know thyself' as a refrain over their wailing forever. Cast: Croesus, Pluto, Menippus, Midas, Sardanapalus.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. Three deposed kings huddled on stone steps under dark columns — Croesus in faded purple, Midas clutching at nothing where gold once was, Sardanapalus draped languidly, all mid-wail. Menippus stands behind them, bald, patched cloak, faint smile, mid-song. Pluto looms at the side on a low throne, chin in hand, deeply unbothered. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar sits between Menippus's feet. Warm torch-light, deep navy gloom.

title: Part Man, Part God, Fully Dead
description: Menippus interrogates two hero-oracles, Trophonius and Amphilochus, about the franchise they're still running upstairs. Trophonius gamely defends his status as a 'hero' — part man, part god — until Menippus points out that one half is allegedly off prophesying in Boeotia while the other half is visibly a corpse. The metaphysics do not survive the conversation. Cast: Menippus, Amphilochus, Trophonius.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. A low cave-mouth set into dark stone columns, lit from within by amber torchlight. Two robed shades — Trophonius in linen oracle-robes, Amphilochus more austere — stand awkwardly at the entrance, half-dignified, half-embarrassed. Menippus faces them with arms folded, faint smile, patched cloak. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar sniffs at a barley-cake on the ground. Deep navy shadow around the frame.

title: Charon's Receipts
description: Hermes sits Charon down to reconcile the books: anchor, oar-strap, sail needle, wax, nails. Charon can't pay until business picks up — meaning, until there's a plague or a decent war. Hermes notes for the record that the modern dead are softer than the old breed: poisoned by wives, bloated by luxury, and almost all here over money. Cast: Hermes, Charon.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. The ferry pulled up on a black pebbled shore. Hermes — light-tenor middle-manager type, neat tunic, winged sandals, stylus and wax tablet in hand — runs down a ledger. Charon, weathered bass ferryman in a stained tunic, leans on his pole looking long-suffering. The leaky boat behind them with visible patches. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar inspects a coil of rope. Warm torch-light against deep navy water.

title: Let the Old Man Live
description: Pluto has an idea for Hermes: let rich, childless Eucrates live another ninety years, and fetch his legacy-hunters down ahead of him. The flatterers have already divvied up the estate in their heads; the punchline is that Eucrates will outlive every one of them and attend their funerals looking younger every year. Hermes approves. Cast: Pluto, Hermes.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. Pluto on a low stone throne, deep authoritative baritone made visible — calm, weary, half-amused. Hermes beside him with a scroll listing seven names. Behind them, a translucent vignette of an ancient rich man in his bed, eyes bright with mischief, surrounded by faint hovering shades of young flatterers. Dark stone columns, warm torch-light, deep navy. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar dozes by Pluto's foot.

title: Dead at Thirty
description: Terpsion arrives at thirty, worn out from worrying about whether ninety-year-old Thucritus would ever finally die. Pluto explains, kindly, that the system is more intelligent than the legacy-hunters give it credit for: the public loves watching them get buried first. Terpsion, slowly, recognises he was the punchline. He still hopes a few rivals predecease Thucritus too. Cast: Terpsion, Pluto.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. A tense, querulous young man in a plain tunic, mid-30s, slightly hollowed out, standing before Pluto's seat between dark stone columns. He clutches a worn ledger of expenses. Pluto leans forward slightly, not unkind, hearing him out. In a small painted panel behind, an ancient grinning old man laughs at a fresh grave. Warm torch-light against deep navy. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar watches from the side.

title: The Wrong Cup
description: Callidemides tells Zenophantus, who himself died choking at his patron's table, how he died: he poisoned a cup for old Ptoeodorus, the wine-pourer muddled the order, and Callidemides drank his own poison. Ptoeodorus laughed. Zenophantus also laughs, then suggests, gently, that the main road would have got him to the inheritance more safely. Cast: Zenophantus, Callidemides.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. Two well-fed shades reclining on stone benches between dark columns, like dinner guests at the worst symposium. Callidemides, dry sardonic baritone made visible, mimes the cup-swap with both hands. Zenophantus, comfortably rotund, is laughing into his fist. A small painted inset shows an old man chuckling over a corpse on a dining-room floor. Warm torch-light, deep navy. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar laps at a spilled cup.

title: The Fawn Hunts the Lion
description: Cnemon explains to Damasias how he drew up a public will leaving everything to wealthy childless Hermolaus, expecting reciprocity. The roof then fell in on Cnemon. Hermolaus has the lot. A short, brisk farce: Cnemon out-schemed himself. Cast: Cnemon, Damasias.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. Cnemon, stunned and rumpled, holds a torn will between dark stone columns. Damasias stands beside him, head tilted, half-sympathetic, half-amused. Above them, a faint painted vignette of a collapsing roof beam. Warm torch-light catches dust still hanging in the air. Deep navy shadow. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar trots past in the foreground, indifferent.

title: Ninety-Eight and Adored
description: Simylus is astonished to learn that Polystratus, the notorious tightwad he remembered, spent his last thirty years being fawned over by lovers — rich, bald, dribbling — competing for a place in the will. Polystratus left everything to a twenty-year-old Phrygian he'd just bought, who is now considered better-born than Codrus. Simylus, eventually, approves. Cast: Simylus, Polystratus.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. An extremely old shade, twinkling-eyed and reedy, sits at ease on a low stone bench. Simylus, plain and worn, leans in, incredulous. Behind them, a faint painted frieze of bald wealthy suitors lined up bearing gifts, and at the far edge a young Phrygian boy with a smooth shaved chin holding a deed. Warm torch-light against deep navy. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar wags its tail at the boy.

title: Strip Before Boarding
description: Charon's boat is overloaded, so Hermes runs a stripping inspection on the gangway. Lampichus the tyrant surrenders his diadem, cruelty, and rage item by item; Damasias the wrestler sheds his flesh and victory wreaths; Craton gives up the family monument; an unnamed philosopher is found to be packing gold, vices, and a five-pound beard, which Menippus chops off with an axe. The rhetorician complies in one line. Cast: Charon, Hermes, Menippus, Lampichus, Damasias, Craton, The Philosopher, The Rhetorician.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. A crowded gangway under dark stone columns. Hermes inspects a queue: Lampichus in stripped-down purple, a massive wrestler shedding wreaths, a soft rich man dropping a tiny model tomb, a pompous bearded philosopher mid-shear with gold coins spilling from his cloak. Menippus stands grinning with a shipwright's axe. Charon's leaky boat waits behind. Warm torch-light against deep navy. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar guards the discarded pile.

title: Wisdom, Self-Sufficiency, Truth
description: Crates tells Diogenes about two cousins, Moerichus and Aristeas, who spent years buttering each other up for mutual inheritance and then died on the same day in the same shipwreck. The estates went to relatives who hadn't seen it coming. Diogenes and Crates compare notes on the only inheritance that matters: wild-olive sticks, satchels, lupins, and plain speech. Cast: Crates, Diogenes.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. Two older Cynics seated on bare stone steps between dark columns — Crates the warm raconteur, Diogenes the gravelly elder — a wild-olive staff propped between them and a worn satchel at their feet. In a small painted panel above, two well-dressed shades sink together beneath stylised waves. Warm torch-light against deep navy. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar sleeps on the satchel.

title: Alexander, Hannibal, Scipio
description: A formal set-piece in Minos's court: Alexander and Hannibal argue precedence, with real competitive heat. Hannibal makes the most self-made case — no divine parents, no fake gods, just the Alps and the Po and rings measured in bushels. Alexander answers with the Granicus, the Ocean, and Porus. Scipio steps in late, concedes to Alexander, and quietly demolishes Hannibal's claim. Minos ranks them and moves on. Cast: Alexander, Hannibal, Minos, Scipio.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. A formal tribunal between dark stone columns. Minos seated centre, resonant and judicial, scroll across his knees. Alexander in a gleaming cuirass and diadem at left, ringing tenor mid-gesture. Hannibal at right, hard clipped baritone, scarred and weathered in foreign cut. Scipio entering at the side in measured Roman dress. Warm torch-light against deep navy. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar watches from the steps.

title: Son of Ammon
description: Diogenes greets Alexander with 'so you're dead too' and proceeds to dismantle the divine-parentage story, the unburied corpse still lying in Babylon, and the Egyptian godhood Ptolemy is allegedly arranging. Alexander weeps about Aristotle's flattery; Diogenes prescribes long draughts from Lethe and points out that Cleitus and Callisthenes are already heading this way. Cast: Diogenes, Alexander.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. Alexander, late 20s, in tarnished purple with the diadem askew, sits on a low step looking genuinely wretched, tears catching the torchlight. Diogenes stands over him, blunt and unsentimental, gesturing to a slow black river beyond the columns. In the deep background, faint approaching shades of murdered courtiers. Warm torch-light against deep navy. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar laps from the river of Lethe.

title: Philip Has Notes
description: Alexander's father takes him through the campaign, item by item, with paternal exasperation: Medes in soft slippers were not real opponents, the kandys and tiara were embarrassing, the dinner-party murders unforgivable. The one thing Philip approves of is Alexander's restraint with Darius's family. The being-a-god routine, Philip notes, fell apart every time Alexander got wounded. Cast: Philip, Alexander.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. A weathered older king in a plain soldier's cloak sits opposite his son between dark columns. Alexander, younger, more brittle, half-turned away, diadem in his lap. Philip's expression is dry, unsentimental, a faint sad smile. Warm torch-light raking across both faces; deep navy behind. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar sits between them like a referee.

title: I'd Rather Be a Hired Hand
description: Achilles tells Antilochus, plainly and quietly, that he regrets the choice: the glory is useless and the dead are all equal under the same gloom. Antilochus does not indulge him — he points out that everyone here is in the same situation, including Heracles and Meleager, and that the others bear it in silence rather than make wishes that get laughed at. The pathos is real. Cast: Antilochus, Achilles.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. Two young heroes seated low on dark stone, armour set aside. Achilles, early 20s, head bowed, the brightness gone from his face, hands loose. Antilochus beside him, calm and steady, one hand near his friend's shoulder but not quite touching. Muted torch-light, very deep navy shadow, the most still and tender composition in the series. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar lies quietly at a respectful distance.

title: Heracles, More or Less
description: Diogenes spots Heracles in the underworld and asks the obvious question: how can the son of Zeus be a corpse? Heracles explains he is only the shade — the real Heracles is upstairs married to Hebe. Diogenes ties him in metaphysical knots until there are three Heracleses and one extra father to account for. Heracles reaches for his bow. Cast: Diogenes, Heracles.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. A massive shade in a lion-skin, bow half-raised, club at his side — bass-baritone bluster made visible. Opposite him, gravelly old Diogenes, completely unimpressed, counting Heracleses on his fingers. Dark stone columns framing them; warm torch-light catching the lion-skin's gold. Deep navy shadow. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar bristles at the lion-skin, unimpressed.

title: Thirsty Without a Mouth
description: Menippus finds Tantalus weeping by the lake and asks the practical question: what does a soul without a body need a drink for? Tantalus explains that this is precisely the punishment — to thirst as though he had a body. Menippus, gently and without mockery, observes that the problem appears to be the wanting, not the water. The pathos is real; the practicality is the comedy. Cast: Menippus, Tantalus.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. Tantalus kneels at the edge of a dark still lake, parched and hollow-cheeked, water visibly receding from his cupped hands. Menippus crouches beside him, patched cloak, faint patient smile, not unkind. Dark stone columns frame the lake. Warm torch-light on the water's retreating ripple. Deep navy beyond. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar sits politely back from the water's edge.

title: A Skull Called Helen
description: Menippus asks Hermes for the celebrity tour — Hyacinthus, Narcissus, Nireus, Helen. Hermes points out a skull. Menippus is unimpressed: this is what a thousand ships were filled for. Hermes, on the clock, briefly defends Homer's verdict, then excuses himself to collect the next batch of dead. Cast: Menippus, Hermes.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. A long shelf of identical skulls arrayed between dark stone columns, faint name-tags barely visible. Menippus, patched cloak and faint smile, lifts one skull to eye level. Hermes beside him, half-turned away, already moving on to the next task, winged sandals mid-step. Warm torch-light, deep navy gloom. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar inspects a fallen jawbone.

title: Strangling in Order
description: Protesilaus is found strangling Helen at the gate. Aeacus calmly redirects him: blame Menelaus. Menelaus redirects him to Paris. Paris pleads Eros, that mandatory god. Aeacus answers on Eros's behalf and points out that Protesilaus jumped first onto the Trojan beach, recklessly, all by himself. Protesilaus, cornered, blames Fate — which Aeacus, fairly, accepts. Cast: Aeacus, Protesilaus, Menelaus, Paris.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. A chaotic but composed group: Protesilaus, young and earnest, hands still half-raised from a strangling pose; Helen as a skull beside him on the floor. Menelaus pointing at Paris; Paris with a charming, slippery half-smile, palms up in innocence. Aeacus in the centre with a functionary's scroll, calmly redirecting. Dark stone columns, warm torch-light, deep navy. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar watches with its head cocked.

title: The Grand Tour
description: Aeacus walks Menippus through the underworld's celebrity wing. Heroes are dust. Pythagoras immediately asks for beans. Empedocles arrives charred from Etna and blames melancholy; Menippus corrects him: vanity. Socrates is across the way, still chatting up beautiful young men. He is the one philosopher who is genuinely at home. Cast: Menippus, Aeacus, Pythagoras, Empedocles, Socrates.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. A long colonnade of dark stone with several pockets of activity. Aeacus leads Menippus past a panel of identical skulls, then past Pythagoras reaching greedily for a satchel of beans, then past a half-charred Empedocles still smoking faintly, then to Socrates seated among bald shades in animated conversation. Warm torch-light against deep navy. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar trots behind Menippus, tail up.

title: Cerberus on Socrates
description: Menippus, dog to dog, gets the inside story from Cerberus. Socrates was brave at the threshold — for the audience — and then wept like an infant once he saw the dark. Cerberus extends the verdict to all of them: bold outside, undone inside. Only Menippus and Diogenes came down laughing, of their own accord. Cast: Menippus, Cerberus.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. A vast three-headed hound, dark-furred and uncanny but not monstrous, lies sphinx-like across a threshold of black stone. Menippus crouches beside one of the heads, conversational, patched cloak, faint smile. In a small painted vignette above the threshold, Socrates is shown both bold-faced outside and weeping inside. Warm torch-light against deep navy. The little Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar sits respectfully beside Cerberus, dwarfed.

title: No Obol
description: Charon tries to collect from Menippus, who has nothing, did not bring anything, bailed the boat himself, and was the only passenger not crying. Hermes refuses to cover the fare. Charon threatens the pole; Menippus offers to crack his skull. They settle on lupins and the leftovers of Hecate's supper, and Menippus walks off whistling. Cast: Charon, Menippus, Hermes.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. Charon on the bank, gruff and exasperated, pole half-raised. Menippus, patched cloak, satchel slung over one shoulder, calmly turning out lupin beans into Charon's palm. Hermes behind, arms folded, refusing to get involved. The leaky boat in the background. Warm torch-light against deep navy water. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar, of course, sits in the best seat on the boat.

title: One Day for Protesilaus
description: Protesilaus petitions Pluto for a single day back in the light — not for life, but for the bride he left on his wedding night. Pluto cites precedent against it; Protesilaus cites Eurydice and Alcestis. Persephone, quietly, solves the problem: have Hermes touch him with the wand and restore him to the bridegroom he was. Pluto agrees. One day. Cast: Protesilaus, Pluto, Persephone.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. A young shade kneels before two thrones between dark stone columns. Pluto, weary baritone in dark robes, leans on one hand. Persephone beside him, warm-eyed mezzo, leaning forward with quiet authority — her gesture is the focal point. Protesilaus's face is half-skull, half-young-man, mid-transformation. Warm torch-light catches Persephone's hand. Deep navy beyond. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar sits at the foot of the throne, unusually still.

title: The Tomb Is in Halicarnassus
description: Mausolus claims top billing on the basis of his kingdom, his looks, and the largest tomb in the known world. Diogenes points out that the tomb is in Halicarnassus and Mausolus is here — so the marble isn't actually doing him any good, except possibly weighing him down. Diogenes doesn't know whether he has a tomb at all. He wasn't interested. Cast: Diogenes, Mausolus.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. Mausolus, richly draped, gestures up at a small painted vignette of an enormous ornate tomb floating in the upper corner of the frame — and the vignette is clearly elsewhere, far away. Diogenes opposite, weathered and amused, holds up two identical skulls for comparison. Dark stone columns, warm torch-light, deep navy. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar pees, decorously off-frame, in the direction of the tomb.

title: Nireus and Thersites
description: Nireus, Homer's handsomest Greek, demands that Menippus judge him better-looking than ugly Thersites. Menippus inspects both skulls and finds Nireus's the more brittle, but otherwise indistinguishable. The famous beauty is outraged. Thersites is, for the first time in his existence, satisfied. Cast: Nireus, Menippus, Thersites.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. Two skulls on a dark stone slab, side by side, lit identically. Behind them, two shades: Nireus a vain young tenor with a faint petulant pout, Thersites coarser and grinning ear to ear. Menippus between them, patched cloak, holding both skulls aloft like a butcher weighing meat. Warm torch-light against deep navy. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar grins along with Thersites.

title: Chiron Chooses Down
description: Menippus asks Chiron why a god chose to die. Chiron explains, calmly: immortality became repetition, and pleasure depends on going without. The underworld is fine — equality is democratic, no hunger, no thirst. Menippus, gently, points out that sameness down here will eventually wear him out too, and there's no third option on offer. Chiron asks what to do. Menippus tells him: be content. Cast: Menippus, Chiron.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. Chiron, depicted here as a noble human-form shade with the faintest suggestion of a centaur's posture, seated on a dark stone bench in conversation with Menippus. Both unhurried, both half-smiling. Warm torch-light, deep navy. The composition is calmer and more spacious than the rest of the series — the show's one genuine exchange between equals. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar rests its head on Chiron's foot.

title: The Old Man Who Wanted to Live
description: The three Cynics gather at the entrance to watch the new arrivals. Crates tells the story of his own crossing — a murdered rich man, a satrap demanding his dead horse, an Armenian who couldn't walk on his soft feet. Antisthenes confesses he ran ahead to bag the best seat on the ferry. Then Diogenes interviews a ninety-year-old beggar — no wealth, no health, no family — who is weeping because the light was sweet. Nobody has a comeback. Cast: Diogenes, Antisthenes, Crates, The Old Pauper.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. Three Cynics — Diogenes, Antisthenes, Crates — leaning against a dark column at the entrance, watching a procession of weeping new arrivals pass. In the foreground, a tiny ancient pauper in rags, leaning on a fishing rod, tears catching the torchlight. The Cynics' faces are quiet, momentarily disarmed. Warm torch-light against deep navy. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar sits at the pauper's feet, ears down.

title: Tiresias, Under Cross-Examination
description: Menippus subjects the blind prophet to relentless anatomical questioning about his stretch as a woman: did he have a womb, did it disappear, did the beard come in gradually or all at once. Tiresias retreats to his standard story about settling a dispute among the gods. Menippus diagnoses the professional habit: none of them can manage a straight word. Cast: Menippus, Tiresias.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. A very old shade with empty eye-sockets and a long staff stands stiffly between dark stone columns, increasingly affronted. Menippus opposite, patched cloak, faint smile, ticking off questions on his fingers with a deadpan curiosity. Warm torch-light against deep navy. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar tilts its head, also waiting for a straight answer.

title: Ajax Will Not Speak to Him
description: Agamemnon tries to mediate between Ajax and the memory of Odysseus, who recently came down to consult the oracle and got cut dead. Ajax restates the grievance over Achilles' armour with undimmed heat: Odysseus was the only one who contested it. Agamemnon, weary, points out that Odysseus won fair, in front of Trojan judges. Ajax is unmoved. Not even Athena could order him to forgive. Cast: Agamemnon, Ajax.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. Two heroes on a dark stone bench between columns. Agamemnon, commanding baritone made visible, gestures patiently. Ajax, hard-jawed and built for war, stares straight ahead, refusing to look across — the low vibration of anger in his shoulders. Above them, a faint painted vignette of Achilles' armour. Warm torch-light against deep navy. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar gives Ajax a wide berth.

title: Sostratus Argues His Way Out
description: Minos has finished assigning punishments — Pyriphlegethon, Chimaera, vultures — when Sostratus the bandit asks for a moment. He walks Minos through it step by step: if Fate spun out all his actions, then he was Clotho's instrument, the way a sword is the judge's. Minos, after a long pause, lets him go and quietly asks him not to teach the rest of the dead the same questions. The collection closes on the underworld's justice quietly conceding a point. Cast: Minos, Sostratus.
artwork_description: Square painterly oil. Minos on his judgment seat between dark stone columns, scroll across his knees, weighing a long pause. Sostratus before him — sharp-eyed, mid-30s, plainly dressed, a quick intelligent baritone made visible — mid-question, one hand open. Behind them, a queue of other dead waiting, fading into deep navy. Warm torch-light catches Minos's slow, dawning half-smile. The Cynic dog with brass-lantern collar sits centre-frame, looking directly at the viewer — the show signing off.
